title: Revisiting Redundancy in Diffusion Transformers: A Temporal-Spatial Joint Caching Strategy for Efficient Sampling

problem.claim: Diffusion Transformers achieve strong generative performance but have significant inference latency.

gap.claim: Existing feature-caching acceleration methods largely ignore dynamic, inconsistent temporal redundancy and underexplore spatial redundancy between adjacent transformer blocks within the same timestep.

contributions.claim: A training-free Temporal-Spatial Joint Cache strategy dynamically determines reuse operations across temporal and spatial dimensions.
A redundancy-guided operation selector uses second-order divided differences to estimate local feature stability and choose among full computation, temporal caching, and spatial caching.
The approach combines interpolation-based feature prediction with bounded cache-distance control to improve reuse accuracy and mitigate error accumulation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish spatial redundancy within the same timestep as a previously underexplored form of efficiency and present a joint temporal-spatial caching perspective.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report substantial inference speedups without retraining or compromising generation fidelity.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion Transformers provide strong generation quality but incur high inference latency.
Prior feature-caching methods overlook dynamic temporal redundancy and spatial redundancy across adjacent blocks.
The proposed Temporal-Spatial Joint Cache dynamically selects reuse operations across temporal and spatial dimensions.
Interpolation-based prediction improves reuse accuracy, while bounded cache distance limits error accumulation.
The authors report speedups without retraining or reduced generation fidelity.
